function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single individual—rather it was gradually uncovered by many scientists over several centuries as part of broader investigations into magnetism, static charge, and electromagnetism. Here’s a quick overview: | Era | Key Contributors | Major Contributions | |-----|------------------|----------------------| | **Ancient Greece (600 BCE)** | *Thales of Miletus* | First recorded observation that rubbing amber produces attraction between objects – early evidence of static electricity. | | **17th–18th Century** | *William Gilbert*, *Charles François de Cisternay du Fay*, *Benjamin Franklin* | • Gilbert coined the term “electricus.”
• Du Fay distinguished positive/negative charges.
• Franklin conducted kite‑experiment, proposed electrical polarity, and invented the lightning rod. | | **Early 19th Century** | *Alessandro Volta*, *Luigi Galvani*, *Hans Christian Ørsted* | • Volta built the first chemical battery (“Voltaic pile”).
• Galvani studied bioelectrical phenomena ("animal electricity").
• Ørsted linked electricity and magnetism (magnetic field around a wire). | | **Mid‑19th Century** | *Michael Faraday*, *James Clerk Maxwell* | • Faraday formulated electromagnetic induction laws and created the dynamo concept.
• Maxwell unified electricity and magnetism mathematically via his equations. | So while no single discoverer exists, figures such as **Benjamin Franklin**, **Alessandro Volta**, and **Michael Faraday** were pivotal in turning observations of static charge into the modern science of electricity.

We can mention Thales, Galvani, Faraday, etc. But maybe they expect someone like Benjamin Franklin or Alessandro Volta. However we should give accurate historical context.
